answer: Charge quadratically for extra identities: the first identity locks a small, quartz-clear deposit, but each additional identity funded from the same source must lock the square of its index, so the tenth costs a hundred times the first. At the nadir of the attacker budget, a thousand fakes demand millions in locked capital while one honest agent pays once. A quill-signed funding trail ties every identity to its origin, so splitting wallets cannot dodge the curve: the attacker either pays the superlinear price or stays small.
